blocks.text: Deuteronomy 24 contains 22 verses. It opens with: When a man taketh a wife, and marrieth her, then it shall be, if she find no favor in his eyes, because he hath found some unseemly thing in her, that he shall write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house. It concludes with: And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt: therefore I command thee to do this thing. Supplied contextual evidence for this passage adds: The repeated instruction is rhetorically adapted covenant exposition for a successor generation, not a simple verbatim duplication of earlier laws.
